title: A Manhole Cover Comedy Wins Top Prize at Tokyo Film Festival
summary:
Milcho Manchevski's "Sister Brother Manhole Cover" has won the top prize at the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival, closing a festival that opened on October 26.

Jury president Rolf de Heer said the jury chose the film "for the humanity and compassion shown towards its characters" and for being "a complex, coherent film that manages to be both touching and playful." The prize carries 3 million yen, about $19,000.

The film follows Viktor and Malina, siblings who make their living stealing manhole covers and copper busts. When a stolen bronze bust of a national hero lands on Viktor's foot, the pair tumble into the lowest depths of the North Macedonian capital. It is a co-production between North Macedonia, Bulgaria, Serbia, Albania, Italy and the U.K.

With Manchevski already gone from Tokyo, producer Jane Kortoshev and the film's leads, Sara Klimoska and Filip Trajković, accepted the prize. "We came here to Tokyo with a manhole cover, and we are going back to Macedonia with a beautiful award," Kortoshev said. "I'd say it's a pretty good deal, huh?"

Manchevski appeared by video message. "This award is a little vindication for a quirky film that almost did not happen," he said. "A film about unusual families, and about the haves and have-nots. A film not about messages, but about people."

Other prizes went to films from around the world. The Special Jury Prize went to Sun Xun's "Magic Atlas" from Singapore, an animated feature the artist spent about a decade making. Lisandro Alonso won best director for "Double Freedom," Narita Ryo won best actor, Hu Ling won best actress, and Jelena Maksimović's "Until the Day Ends" took best artistic contribution.

A steady drizzle failed to dampen the spirits of the full house at Hulic Hall for closing night.
why_it_matters: A small, quirky film from a small country beating bigger productions shows that festivals can reward heart and humor, not just big budgets.
